key_concepts: Simple machines can change the direction and size of forces
A lever has a fulcrum, resistance, and effort
Lever class depends on the relative positions of fulcrum, effort, and resistance
Work is done when a force moves an object over a distance
Effort force is the input force applied by the user
Resistance force is the output force exerted by the machine
Mechanical advantage is the ratio of output force to input force
A mechanical advantage of 1 changes direction without multiplying force
A mechanical advantage greater than 1 multiplies force
A mechanical advantage less than 1 increases speed
Pulley systems can multiply force as the number of pulleys increases
Wheel-and-axle mechanical advantage equals wheel radius divided by axle radius
